coverage.assessment: Two links are cut. The party's influence on the boy (1848–1854) is gone, and so is the explanation of why the four tools mattered. The punctuation joke, Webster's flaming sword and the four tools with mathematics first all survive.

'He stood alone' is moved after the faculties passage, losing what he stood apart from. 'From the one as from the other' lacks its Boston Whig parallel, which was cut in the first draft. The four men, the Mount Vernon Street centre and the library alcove all remain clear.
The chapter has no performed dialogue. Reported speech, such as the father's punctuation complaint, stays correctly attributed.

The Puritan argument loses its corrective clause, so 'So they were' becomes an unqualified concession. The hedged 'No doubt' sentences in the poise passage are retained, satisfying the plan's stated risk. The continuity facts (fourth child, ten to sixteen, laughed till he choked, three besides Mr. Adams) are intact.
The retrospective irony survives in 'Time and experience' and 'as afterwards appeared.' No London achievements are disclosed, and nothing hints at the Sumner rupture.

Signature paradoxes are trimmed: 'hatred of school methods was almost a method in itself,' 'rather an atmosphere than an influence,' and the illustration 'Napoleons and Andrew Jacksons amuse it.' Double hyphens and the long periodic sentences are kept.

Four contrasts are weakened. The pilotage contrast loses its cost. Government-by-the-best loses its Mount Vernon offshoot. Sumner's portrait ends on glacial solitude rather than real superiority. The Puritan 'stamp' argument loses its turn.
All five dependencies have surviving local endpoints and partner endpoints in this run's drafts of 006, 009, 010, 007 and 027.

findings.claim: The revision keeps the clear channel and the unknown ocean. It cuts the father's task (the slave-power) and the bitter consequence that the sons would 'pay for the pilotage' with lives or wasted energies. The first draft had kept both.
findings.counterevidence: The 1840–1870 / 1870–1900 generational contrast still implies that the old pilotage will not serve.

evidence.quote: he might be content to let his sons pay for the pilotage; and it mattered little to his success whether they paid it with their lives wasted on battle-fields

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the sentence 'The task done, he might be content to let his sons pay for the pilotage; and it mattered little...' before the generations sentence.
findings.plan_relation: Plan essential: 'Pilotage: the father's channel was clear, the sons faced an unknown ocean.' The cost clause is not required but carries the point.
findings.reader_effect: The image becomes a neutral contrast instead of an indictment of what the father's success cost his sons. That indictment is the chapter's link between inheritance and failed education.
findings.title: Pilotage loses the cost borne by the sons

The portrait now ends on solitude that 'reacted on his character' and then turns directly to the boy's worship.

findings.claim: In the source, 'He stood alone' follows Mr. Adams's distance from the Unitarian clergy, the Websterian literary group and science. The revision deletes that paragraph and moves the three sentences after 'Within its range it was a model.'

findings.reader_effect: Standing alone now reads as a trait of his mind rather than his position in Boston society. The 'no master, no scholars' antitheses still land.
findings.title: 'He stood alone' detached from the Boston groups it refers to

findings.claim: The revision cuts 'He could not be convinced that moral standards had nothing to do with it, and that utilitarian morality was good enough for him.' 'So they were' now runs straight into Henry's churchly nature. The revision also drops 'There was never a side-path of escape' and 1848 being 'decisive for twenty years.'

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the 'He could not be convinced...' sentence after 'So they were.'
findings.plan_relation: Plan essential: 'The Puritan resists change, believing his standards higher; "So they were."' The reversal that follows is integral to that unit.
findings.reader_effect: The dry concession was meant to be followed by the Puritan's error: the issue was not morality at all. Without it, the reasoning about why the Puritan could not take the new stamp is lost, and the passage reads as simple endorsement of the old standards.
findings.title: Puritan argument loses its corrective turn after 'So they were'

findings.claim: The revision cuts three things the first draft kept. Two are from the school passage: 'The passionate hatred of school methods was almost a method in itself' and the reason for the hatred (a crowd of boys, rote memory). The third explains why the four tools mattered: 'With these, he could master in very short time any special branch of inquiry.'

strengths: All eight verbatim passages (V1–V8) survive intact, including the long V5 hyperbole and the V7 mind-as-machine line.
The optional quatrain is removed, and the sentence before it now ends on a period, as the plan requires.
The poise passage keeps both hedged 'No doubt' sentences, V3, and the Webster/Garrison middle path ending 'set up a party of his own.'
The revision fixes two first-draft glitches: the dangling 'He, too, adored English standards' and the misstated 'opposite defect from his father's restlessness.'
Continuity holds throughout: Henry as fourth child 'of less account,' 'laughed over a witticism till he choked,' 'from ten to sixteen,' and no London achievements stated.
summary: The revision keeps all eight verbatim passages, the continuity facts and every planned dependency. It also repairs two first-draft glitches: the dangling 'He, too, adored' and the garbled 'opposite defect from his father's restlessness.' Its new cuts remove several argumentative hinges. These are the sons paying for the father's pilotage, the party's formative effect on the boy in 1848–1854, the Mount Vernon group as 'statesmen, not politicians,' Sumner's 'real and incontestable' superiority, the Puritan's mistaken belief that morals were the issue, and the school-hatred paradox. None of these is a blocker, but each thins the argument the plan marks as essential. One first-draft referent weakness remains in the library passage.
